verse: Be still, and know that I am God.
insight: Calvin: stillness is not idleness but the soul's posture before sovereignty. While you wait, remember Who runs the universe — and Who does not need your hurry.

verse: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
insight: Before any code compiled, there was the Logos. Every act of naming and ordering you do is a small echo of Genesis 1.

verse: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
insight: Spurgeon: 'I shall not want' is the conclusion of a syllogism whose premise is the Shepherd. The Shepherd determines the supply, not your shortage.

verse: For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be glory forever. Amen.
insight: Edwards: God's end in creation is the communication of His own glory. Your work, however small, is a tributary to that ocean.

verse: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men.
insight: Luther: the milkmaid milking and the magistrate ruling both glorify God if done by faith. So does the engineer debugging.

verse: He must increase, but I must decrease.
insight: Keller: the gospel is not advice but news — news that frees you from needing to be the hero of your own story today.

verse: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.
insight: Trust is not the absence of thought but the refusal to make your own understanding the final court. Submit your reasoning, don't suspend it.

verse: Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
insight: Piper: God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in Him — and anxiety is a confession that we are seeking satisfaction elsewhere.

verse: The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases; his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning.
insight: Even on the morning after the worst commit of your career, the mercies are new. Yesterday's failures do not deplete today's grace.

verse: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
insight: Bonhoeffer: cheap grace is grace without discipleship. The rest Jesus offers is yoked rest — not abdication, but easier yoke.

verse: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.
insight: You are God's poiema — His poem. The good works are pre-prepared; your task is to walk in them, not invent them.

verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the sky above proclaims his handiwork.
insight: All true science is thinking God's thoughts after Him (Kepler). All true craftsmanship is the same in miniature.

verse: Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!
insight: The same Lord who knit you in the womb knows the unrefactored corners of your heart — and is patient with both.

verse: And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good.
insight: All things — including the failing test, the rejected PR, the delayed feature. Providence is not the absence of friction but its repurposing.

verse: But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
insight: Augustine: our hearts are restless until they rest in You. Productivity that does not first seek the Kingdom will not satisfy the seeker.

verse: He has made everything beautiful in its time. Also, he has put eternity into man's heart.
insight: The ache for permanence in your work is a fingerprint of eternity. You were not built only for ship dates.

verse: I can do all things through him who strengthens me.
insight: Read it in context: Paul learned contentment in plenty and in want. The 'all things' is the strength to be faithful in either, not to win every battle.

verse: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
insight: Faith is not a leap into the dark but a step into the light of testimony. The cloud of witnesses cheers you on through this very keystroke.

verse: Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that is set before us.
insight: Endurance is the long obedience in the same direction (Nietzsche, redeemed by Peterson). The race is set — not chosen, not invented — set.

verse: The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face to shine upon you and be gracious to you.
insight: The Aaronic blessing was God's chosen way to put His name on His people. Receive it now, before your next prompt.

verse: Taste and see that the Lord is good!
insight: Edwards distinguished notional from experiential knowledge. You can know about honey or you can taste it. Don't settle for notional Christianity today.

verse: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
insight: The cross is not first a moral example; it is a substitution. The example flows from the substitution, not the other way.

verse: If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.
insight: Union with Christ is the central theological reality of the New Testament (Murray). Not imitation — incorporation.

verse: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.
insight: The Reformation was a recovery of this preposition: 'by' grace — not because of, not alongside, but by. The instrument is faith; the cause is grace.

verse: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge.
insight: Van Til: there are no brute facts. Every datum, including the one in your terminal, presupposes the God who ordained it.

verse: He has told you, O man, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
insight: Three verbs, no nouns of accomplishment. The good life is action: do, love, walk — not having, achieving, optimizing.

verse: Let everything that has breath praise the Lord!
insight: The Psalter ends in a doxology. Whatever you build today, build it toward this telos — a universe of breath returning praise.

verse: I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
insight: Burroughs: contentment is a sweet, inward, quiet, gracious frame of spirit, freely submitting to and delighting in God's wise and fatherly disposal in every condition.

verse: Behold, I am making all things new.
insight: Not all new things, but all things new. Your work is not discarded in the new creation — it is purified and brought in (cf. Rev 21:24-26).

verse: And whatever you do, in word or in deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
insight: The next prompt you send is a 'whatever.' Send it in His name, with thanks, and the most ordinary minute is consecrated.

verse: You will keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts in you.
insight: The Hebrew is 'shalom shalom' — peace, peace. Doubled, perfect, complete. Not the absence of conflict but the presence of God.

verse: It is finished.
insight: Tetelestai — paid in full. The most important work in history is already done. Your work today is response, not requirement.
